# Copilot code review — ascoachingogvaner

Private, **fully static SvelteKit (Svelte 5) + TypeScript** marketing site for a personal coaching practice
(Danish-language content). No database, admin area, or server runtime: the whole site is prerendered with
`@sveltejs/adapter-static` and served by nginx. Deployed as an OCI-packaged Kustomize tenant on the
devantler-tech platform cluster. Canonical conventions live in [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md); this is the
concise review checklist — flag violations of the rules below.

## Always (every PR)

- **Conventional-Commit PR title** (`feat:`/`fix:`/`docs:`/`ci:`/`chore:`/`refactor:`/`test:`). The
  squash-merge title feeds semantic-release, so a non-conventional or bracket-prefixed title is a defect.
- **Root-cause fixes only.** Flag anything that masks a failure instead of fixing it: checks skipped or
  set `continue-on-error` to dodge red CI, deleted/weakened assertions, `--no-verify`, silenced linters.
- **Never hand-edit generated files.** Here: `package-lock.json` (let npm regenerate). Flag manual edits.
- **Behaviour / content / route / config / UX change ⇒ its docs updated in the same PR**
  (`README.md` / `AGENTS.md`). A missing doc update is a review finding.
- **No secrets in plaintext** — flag committed `.env`, tokens, or kubeconfigs. (This site has no secrets;
  all copy, contact details and the external booking URL live in `src/lib/content.ts`.)
- PRs from the Daily AI Assistant carry a `> 🤖 Generated by the Daily AI Assistant` line — expected, not a finding.

## SvelteKit + TypeScript (static)

- Svelte 5 **runes** (`$state`/`$derived`/`$props`); flag legacy `export let` / reactive `$:` in new code.
  Keep TypeScript strict — no new `any`, no `// @ts-ignore` to dodge a real type error.
- The site is **fully prerendered**: `src/routes/+layout.ts` sets `prerender = true` for the whole site.
  Flag anything that breaks static output — server-only code (`+page.server.ts` with runtime logic), `load`
  that needs a request, or a non-static adapter. There is no server at runtime.
- `npm run check` (svelte-kit sync && svelte-check) and `npm run lint` (ESLint flat config,
  `eslint-plugin-svelte` + `typescript-eslint`) must pass — they are required CI checks.
- TailwindCSS v4 (`@tailwindcss/vite`); prefer utility classes over ad-hoc `<style>`.
- Content & contact: copy lives in `src/lib/content.ts`; the contact form builds a `mailto:` link via
  `src/lib/mailto.ts` (no backend). Flag attempts to add a server endpoint or external form POST.
- Unit tests are **Vitest** (`tests/unit/`), E2E is **Playwright** (`tests/e2e/`). New behaviour ⇒ a test;
  don't delete a failing test to go green.

## Accessibility & content

- Public-facing marketing site: keep semantic HTML, alt text on images, and WCAG-AA contrast intact.
- Danish-language content — keep copy in `content.ts`, don't hard-code strings in components.

## Validation & CI

- Run the same checks CI runs (the workflow splits them into separate jobs, each doing `npm ci` + one step):
  `npm ci && npm run lint && npm run check && npm test && npm run test:e2e && npm run build`
  (`build` prerenders to `build/` via adapter-static; the Docker image serves it with nginx).
- Private platform-tenant app — be conservative; never expose its contents publicly.

When unsure, defer to [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) and its `## Maintenance` section.
